thesisQuality.note: Strong cash-earnings execution, high fleet availability and structural PJM load growth support durable demand/value capture, while Helix-specific economics remain unproven.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Q2 adjusted EBITDA rose more than 30% year over year, guidance was reaffirmed, fleet availability was at least 97%, and liquidity was substantial; collateral and leverage sensitivities prevent exceptional-band treatment.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: At roughly $46.5B market cap and about 9.9x EV/EBITDA on September 25, valuation offers plausible headroom against supported 2026/2027 earnings but is not a rare or low-expectation asymmetry.

catalystScore.note: Helix/data-center power optionality, Cogentrix and generation development are identifiable material catalysts, but project timing and realized economics remain uncertain.

governancePower.note: Management has maintained guidance, disclosed capital-market activity and executed substantial multi-year repurchases, but reviewed evidence does not establish exceptional long-duration stewardship.

alignment2036.note: Reliable electricity generation and capacity are foundational infrastructure for multiple future demand paths, with PJM independently projecting structural large-load growth.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: A diversified generation fleet, retail/market exposure and digital-infrastructure power optionality provide several demand channels, though all remain tied to electricity-market economics.

bottleneckControl.note: Existing dispatchable generation and market access participate directly in a region where PJM documents rising load and reliable-capacity pressure; permitting/interconnection and new supply constrain a higher score.

scenarioRobustness.note: Existing fleet serves broad power demand across scenarios, but merchant exposure, collateral needs and evolving large-load reliability rules create meaningful downside paths.

substitutionResilience.note: Reliable generation has near-term qualification and capacity value, but renewables/storage, new gas/nuclear and grid expansion can substitute over time.

supplyChainResilience.note: Fleet breadth and liquidity provide some resilience, but fuel, plant availability, commodity collateral and acquisition/integration dependencies remain material and the reviewed evidence does not establish tested exceptional redundancy.

pricingPower.note: High availability and strong EBITDA show current economic capture amid capacity scarcity, while merchant/hedged market exposure means pricing is not structurally company-controlled.

risk.note: Commodity-market collateral, leverage/refinancing, outages/integration and large-load reliability/interconnection risks are material but balanced by strong liquidity, operating cash earnings and demand evidence.

confidence.note: Identity/tradability are validated and evidence spans issuer, SEC, independent system-operator and fresh independent market sources; project-level Helix economics and some forward valuation assumptions remain unknown.

thesis: Vistra combines scarce reliable generation, strong current operating execution and structural large-load demand exposure, but value realization remains sensitive to merchant power economics, collateral/leverage and whether regional data-center growth converts into durable Vistra-specific contracted economics.
keyRisk: Power-market/collateral stress or reliability/interconnection friction could prevent strong regional demand from converting into expected cash economics while leverage remains meaningful.
nextCatalyst: Next earnings update on 2026/2027 cash-earnings trajectory, Cogentrix/Helix progress and evidence of contracted large-load economics.
